    experiments : pathlib.Path
        The list from :func:`experiment_list`.
    client : EntrezClient
        The Entrez seam; its limiter sets the rate.
    date : str
        The fetch date recorded on every row.
    batch, inflight, part_size : int
        Experiments per call, calls in flight, experiments per part.
    log_every : float
        Seconds between progress lines.
    refetch : iterable of str
        Experiments to fetch again.

    Returns
    -------
    LaneReport
        Counts for this run. An experiment whose call failed is asked once more before the
        lane ends; if that fails too it is saved as an ``sra-fetch-failed`` row, not as a
        package, so the next run asks for it again. A new
        one NCBI has no package for is saved with an empty text and counted in ``missing``.
        Saved bad packages are asked again: ``reasked`` counts them, ``recovered`` those that
        came back good and replace the saved copy. A re-fetch experiment NCBI serves none
        for keeps its saved package and is listed in ``unserved``.
    """
    sizes = (batch, inflight, part_size)
    noted = gaps.noted(root, gaps.UNPARSABLE_PACKAGE)
    again = frozenset(refetch)
    first, settled, failed = _fetch_once(
        root, experiments, client, date, sizes, log_every, noted, set(), again
    )
    report = first
    if first.failed:
        logger.info("asking again for the %d experiments whose calls failed", first.failed)
        last, _, failed = _fetch_once(
            root, experiments, client, date, sizes, log_every, noted, settled, again
        )
        report = LaneReport(
            first.fetched + last.fetched,
            first.missing + last.missing,
            last.failed,
            len(settled) + last.reasked,
            first.recovered + last.recovered,
            first.unserved | last.unserved,
        )
    _record_failed(root, failed, date)
    logger.info(
        "asked again for %d saved bad packages; %d came back good",
        report.reasked,
        report.recovered,
    )
    return report

items.title: raw
items.text:
What raw/ and its parts hold, the only reader and writer of both.

A raw row is accession, raw_text, hash and fetch_date. A source's rows sit in raw/<source>/<bucket>.parquet, a bucket being a range of :data:WIDTHS accession numbers. :func:save writes rows as a part under work/parts/, and :func:remove a removal part; :func:pack merges them into the bucket files, and :func:files hands a build those.

Every read and pack share one merge: the bucket file, then the parts oldest first, the newest row of an accession winning and a removal dropping the rows saved before it. So an accession is held, or left to fetch, alike before and after pack. Writer side only, so pyarrow is imported here freely.

Return the bucket an accession's rows go in within one source.

The bucket keeps the accession's prefix and its number with the last digits of the source's width written n: at width 10,000, GSE246310 -> GSE24nnnn.

def bucket_of(source: str, accession: str) -> str:
    """Return the bucket an accession's rows go in within one source.

    The bucket keeps the accession's prefix and its number with the last digits of the
    source's width written ``n``: at width 10,000, ``GSE246310`` -> ``GSE24nnnn``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the accession is not letters then digits.
    KeyError
        If the source has no width in :data:`WIDTHS`.
    """
    digits = len(str(WIDTHS[source])) - 1
    if match := _ACCESSION.match(accession):
        return f"{match[1]}{match[2][:-digits]}{'n' * digits}"
    raise ValueError(f"no raw bucket for {accession!r}")

def files(root: Path, source: str, scratch: Path | None = None) -> list[Path]:
    """Return Parquet files that hold exactly what a source holds, one per bucket.

    Without ``scratch`` they are the bucket files. With it, a bucket with parts is merged
    into ``scratch``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : pathlib.Path
        The store root.
    source : str
        The raw source.
    scratch : pathlib.Path or None
        The folder merged buckets are written to.

    Returns
    -------
    list of pathlib.Path
        The files, bucket files first.

    Raises
    ------
    StoreBuildError
        Without ``scratch``, if the source has parts left to pack.
    """
    parts = _parts_by_bucket(root, source)
    out = [p for p in sorted(paths.RAW.at(root, source).glob("*.parquet")) if p.stem not in parts]
    if not parts:
        return out
    if scratch is None:
        raise StoreBuildError(
            f"{source} has parts left to pack in {_parts_dir(root, source)}; "
            "run `labdata store pack` first"
        )
    scratch.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for bucket in sorted(parts):
        out.append(scratch / f"{bucket}.parquet")
        found, _ = _layers(root, source, bucket, parts[bucket])
        newer = (row for _, row, _ in _newest_rows(found) if row is not None)
        _write_sorted_runs(out[-1], newer, SCHEMA)
    return out

    refetch: Iterable[str] = (),
) -> list[Piece]

Split accessions into pieces, one per bucket, of those left to fetch.

An accession is left when the source does not hold it, unless a piece since the last removal of it asked for it and got no row. A refetch accession, wanted too, is left unless a row saved since the last pack holds it. A bucket with nothing left yields no piece.

Source code in src/labdata/store/raw.py 
def pieces(
    root: Path, source: str, accessions: Iterable[str], refetch: Iterable[str] = ()
) -> list[Piece]:
    """Split accessions into pieces, one per bucket, of those left to fetch.

    An accession is left when the source does not hold it, unless a piece since the last
    removal of it asked for it and got no row. A ``refetch`` accession, wanted too, is left
    unless a row saved since the last pack holds it. A bucket with nothing left yields no piece.
    """
    again = set(refetch)
    by_bucket: dict[str, set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
    for accession in itertools.chain(accessions, again):
        by_bucket[bucket_of(source, accession)].add(accession)
    parts = _parts_by_bucket(root, source)
    out = []
    for bucket, members in sorted(by_bucket.items()):
        wanted = _Wanted.of(members)
        found, bucket_runs = _layers(
            root, source, bucket, parts.get(bucket, []), (), asked=True, wanted=wanted
        )
        done = {a for a, entries in _merge(found) if _done(entries, bucket_runs, a in again)}
        if left := members - done:
            out.append(Piece(source, bucket, tuple(sorted(left))))
    return out

    root: Path, source: str, accessions: Iterable[str]

Write removal parts deleting these accessions' rows from one source, one per bucket.

A removal drops the rows saved before it, and a row saved after it wins. A removal part already written is left as it is, keeping its place.

Returns:

Source code in src/labdata/store/raw.py 
def remove(root: Path, source: str, accessions: Iterable[str]) -> list[Path]:
    """Write removal parts deleting these accessions' rows from one source, one per bucket.

    A removal drops the rows saved before it, and a row saved after it wins. A removal part
    already written is left as it is, keeping its place.

    Returns
    -------
    list of pathlib.Path
        The removal parts, written or already there.
    """
    by_bucket: dict[str, set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
    for accession in accessions:
        by_bucket[bucket_of(source, accession)].add(accession)
    folder = _parts_dir(root, source)
    written = []
    for bucket, members in sorted(by_bucket.items()):
        listed = "\n".join(sorted(members))
        tag = f"removed-{hashlib.sha256(listed.encode()).hexdigest()[:12]}"
        folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        if kept := _parts_of(folder, bucket, tag):
            written += kept
            continue
        schema = SCHEMA.with_metadata({_REMOVED_KEY: listed.encode()})
        written.append(_write_part_file(folder, bucket, tag, [], schema))
    return written

def save(
    root: Path,
    source: str,
    rows: Iterable[RawRow],
    *,
    asked: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    chunk_bytes: int = SORT_CHUNK_BYTES,
) -> list[Path]:
    """Save rows as parts, one per bucket: a row wins over every older row of its accession.

    ``asked`` lists what one bucket's fetch asked for: the rows stream to one part that
    records them, so one that got no row is not fetched again before the next pack. Without
    it, the rows are held in memory.

    Returns
    -------
    list of pathlib.Path
        The parts written.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a row is not in the bucket of ``asked``.
    """
    if asked is not None:
        piece = Piece(source, bucket_of(source, asked[0]), tuple(asked))
        return [_write_part(root, piece, rows, record_asked=True, chunk_bytes=chunk_bytes)]
    by_bucket: dict[str, list[RawRow]] = defaultdict(list)
    for row in rows:
        by_bucket[bucket_of(source, row.accession)].append(row)
    return [
        _write_part(
            root,
            Piece(source, bucket, tuple(sorted({row.accession for row in chunk}))),
            chunk,
            record_asked=False,
            chunk_bytes=chunk_bytes,
        )
        for bucket, chunk in sorted(by_bucket.items())
    ]

def pack(
    root: Path,
    sources: Iterable[str] | None = None,
    *,
    chunk_bytes: int = SORT_CHUNK_BYTES,
    counts: Path | None = None,
) -> list[Path]:
    """Merge every source's parts into its bucket files and document the folders changed.

    A bucket is rewritten whole by the merge every read uses, its inputs read a few rows at a
    time and written a chunk at a time, so memory holds a chunk, never a bucket or a source.
    A bucket left with no rows is deleted. A bucket file named for another width is first
    split into parts, so a width change repacks the same rows.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : pathlib.Path
        The store root.
    sources : iterable of str or None
        The raw folders to pack; defaults to every source with parts or a bucket file.
    chunk_bytes : int
        Raw text held before a row group is written.
    counts : pathlib.Path or None
        A file to append one JSON line to per bucket rewritten: its source, bucket, the
        parts it took in, and the records :data:`COUNTS` names: added, replaced (held with
        another text) and removed.

    Returns
    -------
    list of pathlib.Path
        The bucket files rewritten or deleted. Each source's count of removed records is logged.
    """
    from labdata.store import provenance  # provenance reads this module's widths

    if sources is None:
        found = {p.name for p in paths.PARTS.at(root).glob("*") if p.is_dir()}
        found |= {p.name for p in paths.RAW.at(root).glob("*") if p.is_dir()}
        sources = sorted(found)
    written: list[Path] = []
    for source in sources:
        done, removed = _pack_source(root, source, chunk_bytes, counts)
        written += done
        if removed:
            logger.info("%s: removed %d record%s", source, removed, "" if removed == 1 else "s")
        if done:
            provenance.document_raw(root, source)
    return written

def gap_row(series: str, reason: str, fetch_date: str, detail: str = "") -> raw.RawRow:
    """Return the ``raw/geo-gaps/`` row recording why the store does not hold a Series.

    Parameters
    ----------
    series : str
        The target Series.
    reason : str
        Any reason but ``UNEXPLAINED``.
    fetch_date : str
        The fetch date.
    detail : str
        One line, such as the last error; optional.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the reason is not a recordable one.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> gap_row("GSE1", SOFT_MISSING, "2026-10-14").raw_text
    'soft-missing'
    """
    if reason not in RECORDED:
        raise ValueError(f"not a recordable gap reason: {reason!r}")
    line = " ".join(detail.split())
    return raw.RawRow(series, f"{reason}\n{line}" if line else reason, fetch_date)

def write_gaps(
    root: Path,
    build_dir: Path,
    target_list: Path,
    date: str,
    fraction: float | None = None,
    *,
    source: targets.BuildSource | None = None,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Write ``gaps.parquet`` from the target list, ``holdings.parquet`` and ``raw/geo-gaps/``.

    ``fraction`` names the round's sample the target list is, so coverage re-reads the same.
    ``raw/`` is read from ``source``, which defaults to ``root``.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        ``snapshot_date``, ``target`` and ``held`` counts, and ``gaps``: the count by reason,
        every reason listed; ``fraction`` too for a round's sample.
    """
    out = GAPS.path(build_dir)
    metadata = {DATE_KEY: date}
    if fraction is not None:
        metadata[FRACTION_KEY] = repr(fraction)
    reasons = ", ".join(sql_string(r) for r in RECORDED)
    with extract.connect(root) as con:
        layout.write(
            con,
            GAPS,
            out,
            f"""WITH g AS ({_gap_rows(root if source is None else source.root)})
            SELECT t.accession,
              CASE WHEN g.reason IN ({reasons}) THEN g.reason ELSE '{UNEXPLAINED}' END
                AS reason,
              CASE WHEN g.reason IS NULL OR g.reason IN ({reasons}) THEN g.detail
                ELSE 'recorded reason: ' || g.reason END AS detail
            FROM (SELECT DISTINCT accession FROM {_read(target_list)}) t
            LEFT JOIN g USING (accession)
            WHERE t.accession NOT IN ({_held_series(build_dir)})""",
            metadata,
        )
        counts = dict(
            con.execute(f"SELECT reason, count(*) FROM {_read(out)} GROUP BY 1").fetchall()
        )
        target = _count(con, f"SELECT count(DISTINCT accession) FROM {_read(target_list)}")
    by_reason = {reason: int(counts.get(reason, 0)) for reason in REASONS}
    summary: dict[str, object] = {"snapshot_date": date}
    if fraction is not None:
        summary["fraction"] = fraction
    return summary | {
        "target": target,
        "held": target - sum(by_reason.values()),
        "gaps": by_reason,
    }

def write_notes(
    root: Path,
    build_dir: Path,
    target_list: Path,
    extra: Iterable[Note] = (),
    *,
    source: targets.BuildSource | None = None,
) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Write ``notes.parquet``: type disagreements, failed package fetches, then ``extra``.

    A failed package fetch is an experiment ``raw/sra-fetch-failed/`` of ``source`` (default
    ``root``) holds and its ``raw/sra-xml/`` does not. When ``source`` samples, only the
    experiments in its seeded sample are noted.

    Returns
    -------
    dict of str to int
        The note count by kind.
    """
    out = NOTES.path(build_dir)
    series = records_path(build_dir, "GEO Series")
    rows = list(extra)
    extra_table = pa.table(
        {
            "accession": [n.accession for n in rows],
            "kind": [n.kind for n in rows],
            "detail": [n.detail for n in rows],
        },
        schema=NOTES.schema(),
    )
    disagree = (
        f"""SELECT t.accession, '{TYPE_DISAGREES}' AS kind,
              'snapshot: ' || t.gdstype || ' | SOFT: ' || coalesce(s.types, 'no type') AS detail
            FROM {_read(target_list)} t
            JOIN (SELECT accession FROM {_read(series)}) r USING (accession)
            LEFT JOIN (
              SELECT accession, string_agg(DISTINCT f.value, '; ' ORDER BY f.value) AS types,
                bool_or(contains(lower(f.value), {sql_string(targets.SEQUENCING)}))
                  AS sequencing
              FROM (SELECT accession, unnest(fields) AS f FROM {_read(series)})
              WHERE f.name = 'Series_type' GROUP BY accession
            ) s USING (accession)
            WHERE NOT coalesce(s.sequencing, false)"""
        if series.is_file()
        else "SELECT * FROM extra WHERE false"
    )
    unfetched = "SELECT * FROM extra WHERE false"
    sample = None if source is None else source.sample
    held_in = root if source is None else source.root
    saved = raw.files(held_in, raw.SRA_XML)
    if failed := raw.files(held_in, raw.SRA_FETCH_FAILED):
        held = (
            f"SELECT accession FROM {read_parquet_sql(saved)}"
            if saved
            else "SELECT NULL::VARCHAR AS accession WHERE false"
        )
        unfetched = (
            f"SELECT accession, '{PACKAGE_FETCH_FAILED}' AS kind, "
            f"'no package saved; a rerun asks again' AS detail FROM {read_parquet_sql(failed)} "
            f"WHERE accession NOT IN ({held})"
            + ("" if sample is None else " AND in_sample(accession)")
        )
    with extract.connect(root) as con:
        con.register("extra", extra_table)
        if sample is not None:
            targets.add_in_sample(con, sample)
        layout.write(
            con, NOTES, out, f"{disagree} UNION ALL {unfetched} UNION ALL SELECT * FROM extra"
        )
        counts = con.execute(f"SELECT kind, count(*) FROM {_read(out)} GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1")
        return {str(kind): int(n) for kind, n in counts.fetchall()}

Check one build against the target list of the snapshot its gaps were made from.

The target list is re-read from the snapshot, so a stale or partial gaps.parquet fails rather than agreeing with itself. A round's build is checked against its sample.

Raises:

def coverage(root: Path, build: BuildReader) -> Coverage:
    """Check one build against the target list of the snapshot its gaps were made from.

    The target list is re-read from the snapshot, so a stale or partial ``gaps.parquet``
    fails rather than agreeing with itself. A round's build is checked against its sample.

    Raises
    ------
    StoreBuildError
        If the build has no ``gaps.parquet`` or its snapshot is gone.
    """
    gaps_file = GAPS.path(build.path)
    if not gaps_file.is_file():
        raise StoreBuildError(f"{build.path} has no {GAPS}; rebuild with `labdata store build`")
    meta = pq.read_metadata(gaps_file).metadata or {}
    date = meta[DATE_KEY.encode()].decode()
    fraction = meta.get(FRACTION_KEY.encode())
    target_list = targets.target_list(root, date, None if fraction is None else float(fraction))
    with extract.connect(root) as con:
        con.execute(f"CREATE VIEW t AS SELECT DISTINCT accession FROM {_read(target_list)}")
        con.execute(f"CREATE VIEW h AS {_held_series(build.path)}")
        con.execute(f"CREATE VIEW g AS SELECT accession, reason, detail FROM {_read(gaps_file)}")
        target = _count(con, "SELECT count(*) FROM t")
        held = _count(con, "SELECT count(*) FROM t WHERE accession IN (SELECT accession FROM h)")
        by_reason = dict(con.execute("SELECT reason, count(*) FROM g GROUP BY 1").fetchall())
        problems = f"""
            SELECT accession, 'not held and no gap row' FROM t
              WHERE accession NOT IN (SELECT accession FROM h)
              AND accession NOT IN (SELECT accession FROM g)
            UNION ALL SELECT accession, 'gap row for a held Series' FROM g
              WHERE accession IN (SELECT accession FROM h)
            UNION ALL SELECT accession, 'gap row for a Series not on the target list' FROM g
              WHERE accession NOT IN (SELECT accession FROM t)
            UNION ALL SELECT accession, '{UNEXPLAINED}' || coalesce(': ' || detail, '') FROM g
              WHERE reason = '{UNEXPLAINED}'"""
        failures = _count(con, f"SELECT count(*) FROM ({problems})")
        failing = con.execute(f"SELECT * FROM ({problems}) ORDER BY 1, 2 LIMIT {NAMED}").fetchall()
        notes = NOTES.path(build.path)
        failed_experiments = (
            _count(
                con,
                f"SELECT count(*) FROM {_read(notes)} WHERE kind = '{PACKAGE_FETCH_FAILED}'",
            )
            if notes.is_file()
            else 0
        )
    return Coverage(
        snapshot_date=date,
        target=target,
        held=held,
        gaps={reason: int(by_reason.get(reason, 0)) for reason in (*REASONS, *by_reason)},
        failing=tuple((str(a), str(p)) for a, p in failing),
        failures=failures,
        failed_experiments=failed_experiments,
    )

items.title: prune
items.text:
Delete the builds and snapshots the store no longer reads, after a grace period.

A non-current build goes once the store switched away from it more than the grace period ago, GRACE by default. A snapshot goes once it is older than the one the current build reads and every build that read it went out of use more than the grace period ago; its extract goes with it. A snapshot newer than the current build's is waiting for the next build and stays. Neither the current build nor what it reads is ever deleted, nor the new build of an update that has not switched to it. Abandoned refresh folders, and what a killed build or step left, go at once.

def prune(
    root: Path,
    *,
    now: dt.datetime | None = None,
    grace: dt.timedelta = GRACE,
    owner_gone: bool = False,
) -> PruneReport:
    """Delete old builds and unread snapshots, keeping everything inside the grace period.

    A build switched away from before switch times were recorded counts as switched away
    when the current build was switched to. After deleting anything, it rewrites the root
    ``README.md`` so its sizes stay current.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : pathlib.Path
        The store root.
    now : datetime.datetime or None
        The time to measure the grace period from; defaults to the current UTC time.
    grace : datetime.timedelta
        How long a build stays after the store switched away from it: ``GRACE``, 24 hours,
        by default. Zero deletes at once.
    owner_gone : bool
        As for :func:`labdata.store.lifecycle.run_lock`.

    Returns
    -------
    PruneReport
        The folders deleted.

    Raises
    ------
    StoreBuildError
        If a build, prune or copy of this store is running, or another update holds the run
        lock.
    """
    with lifecycle.run_lock(root, lifecycle.PRUNE, owner_gone=owner_gone), build_lock(root):
        report = _delete(root, now or dt.datetime.now(dt.UTC), grace)
    # After the locks are released, so the README's sizes leave out the run lock.
    if report.deleted and paths.read_marker(root).get(paths.BUILD_KEY):
        readme.try_write(root)
    return report

def write(root: Path) -> Path:
    """Write ``<root>/README.md`` for the build the marker names.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : pathlib.Path
        The store root.

    Returns
    -------
    pathlib.Path
        The README written.

    Raises
    ------
    NotAStoreError
        If the root has no marker, or the marker names no build.
    """
    settings = paths.read_marker(root)
    folder = current_path(root)
    build = folder.name
    path = manifest_path(folder)
    manifest = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if path.is_file() else {}
    made = manifest.get("produced_by")
    snaps = manifest.get("inputs", {}).get("snapshots", {})
    sizes = [(f"{folder.relative_to(root).as_posix()}/", _size(folder))] + [
        (f"{name}/", _size(root / name)) for name in _SIZED if (root / name).is_dir()
    ]
    text = string.Template(_template()).substitute(
        build=build,
        switched=settings.get(paths.SWITCHED_KEY, "an unrecorded time"),
        made_by=_made_by(made),
        snapshot_table=_table(
            ("Source", "Date", "File"),
            [(f"`{s}`", v["date"], f"`{v['name']}`") for s, v in sorted(snaps.items())],
        ),
        size_table=_table(("Folder", "Size"), [(f"`{n}`", _human(b)) for n, b in sizes]),
    )
    out = paths.README.at(root)
    write_atomic(out, text)
    return out

items.title: gcs
items.text:
Copy the store's current state to GCS, which holds it for good: what changed since the last.

This is the GEO/SRA store's adapter of :mod:labdata._gcs. The held set is the current state: the current build and the raw files and snapshot folders it read, as its manifest names them, with the README and manifest beside each, the marker and the root README.md. work/, support/ and older builds stay behind. The copy record, :data:COPIED, is JSON: each file with its sha256, or null for a file sent every time. :func:labdata.store.lifecycle.finalize runs each copy and gives it the status record to send last, marked finalized.

A routine copy with no copy record on the work disk or in GCS seeds one from the build the marker in GCS names, when GCS is known to hold exactly that build and a listing finds its files there; otherwise it is skipped and asks for labdata store copy --full, which uploads the current state and deletes nothing. A copy refuses, sending nothing, when it would delete more of the copy record's raw files than :func:labdata._gcs.delete_limit allows, unless the deletes are accepted by hand, or when the work disk is not in step with GCS (:func:check). :func:restore fills a work disk from GCS.

def destination(root: Path, to: str | None = None) -> str:
    """Return ``to``, or else the marker's ``copy_to``: where the store's copy goes.

    Raises
    ------
    StoreCopyError
        If ``root`` is not a store, or neither names a destination.
    """
    try:
        store = open_store(root)
    except NotAStoreError as err:
        raise StoreCopyError(f"copy refused: {err}") from None
    dest = str(to or store.settings.get(_gcs.COPY_TO_KEY) or "")
    if not dest:
        raise StoreCopyError(
            f"no destination: pass --to <remote>:<bucket>/<path> or set "
            f"{_gcs.COPY_TO_KEY} in {paths.MARKER.at(root)}"
        )
    return dest

def send(
    root: Path,
    dest: str,
    status: bytes | None,
    *,
    full: bool = False,
    accept_deletes: int = 0,
    bucket_matches_marker: bool = False,
) -> _gcs.CopyResult:
    """Send the store's changes since the last successful copy to ``dest``, then ``status``.

    Holds the build lock; :func:`labdata.store.lifecycle.finalize` runs it.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : pathlib.Path
        The store root.
    dest : str
        An rclone path, ``<remote>:<bucket>/<path>``.
    status : bytes or None
        The status record marked finalized, sent last; None sends none.
    full : bool
        Upload every file of the current state instead, and delete nothing. It lists every
        file on both sides; for a first copy or a repair.
    accept_deletes : int
        Delete up to this many raw files the current build no longer reads, even past the
        usual bound: for files removed on purpose.
    bucket_matches_marker : bool
        Whether GCS holds exactly the build its marker names and what that build read. A
        routine copy with no copy record, on the disk or in GCS, then seeds one from that
        build, if it is on the disk and GCS holds its files with the disk's sizes.

    Returns
    -------
    CopyResult
        ``skipped`` is true, with a message, when rclone's Google login has expired, or when a
        routine copy finds no copy record and cannot seed one.

    Raises
    ------
    StoreCopyError
        If the current build is incomplete, the work disk is not in step with GCS, more of
        the copied raw files would be deleted than this copy deletes, or rclone fails for
        another reason. rclone is not called when the build is incomplete.
    StoreBuildError
        If a build, prune or copy of this store is running.
    """
    with build_lock(root):
        held = _current(root, paths.read_marker(root).get(paths.BUILD_KEY))
        adapter = _Adapter(root, seeds=bucket_matches_marker)
        skipped = _gcs.copy(adapter, dest, held, status, full=full, accept_deletes=accept_deletes)
    return _gcs.CopyResult(dest, skipped=skipped is not None, message=skipped or "")

def restore(
    root: Path, source: str | None = None, *, approve: Callable[[int, int], bool]
) -> str | None:
    """Fill the work disk at ``root`` from ``source``, as :func:`labdata._gcs.restore` says.

    Holds the store's build lock, so a restore never runs beside a build, prune or copy.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : pathlib.Path
        The store root; it may be empty or missing.
    source : str or None
        An rclone path, ``<remote>:<bucket>/<path>``; defaults to the marker's ``copy_to``.
    approve : callable
        Called with the number of files and bytes to download, before any; False stops it.

    Returns
    -------
    str or None
        Why it stopped: rclone's login has expired or ``approve`` said no; None when done.

    Raises
    ------
    StoreCopyError
        If no source is set, GCS holds no copy record or lacks a file it names, or rclone fails.
    StoreBuildError
        If a build, prune or copy of this store is running.
    """
    if not source and paths.MARKER.at(root).is_file():
        source = str(paths.read_marker(root).get(_gcs.COPY_TO_KEY) or "")
    if not source:
        raise StoreCopyError("no source: pass --from <remote>:<bucket>/<path>")
    with build_lock(root):
        return _gcs.restore(_Adapter(root, seeds=False), source, approve=approve)

def check_new_root(root: Path, source: Path, marker: str, subset_of: str, what: str) -> bool:
    """Check that a subset may be written into ``root``; return whether it holds one already.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : pathlib.Path
        The new root.
    source : pathlib.Path
        The root the subset is read from.
    marker : str
        The marker file's name in a root of this kind.
    subset_of : str
        What a subset's marker in ``root`` must name under ``SUBSET_OF_KEY``.
    what : str
        The kind of root, for messages, such as ``"store"``.

    Raises
    ------
    StoreBuildError
        If ``root`` is the source or lies inside it, holds a marker that is not this
        subset's, or holds anything else.
    """
    new, old = root.resolve(), source.resolve()
    if new == old or old in new.parents:
        raise StoreBuildError(
            f"a subset needs a root apart from its source {what}, not {root}; "
            "the source is only read"
        )
    if (root / marker).is_file():
        named = read_toml_marker(root, marker, f"a {what}").get(SUBSET_OF_KEY)
        if named != subset_of:
            was = "is not a subset" if named is None else f"is a subset of {named}"
            raise StoreBuildError(
                f"{root} holds a {what} that {was}, not a subset of {subset_of}; "
                "pick an empty folder"
            )
        return True
    if root.exists() and (not root.is_dir() or any(root.iterdir())):
        raise StoreBuildError(f"{root} is not empty and is not a subset; pick an empty folder")
    return False

The new build holds the listed Series the source holds, and every record reached from them over FOLLOWED, step after step, with the parent of each held BioProject. It keeps every link row with a held record at an end, and every link row of a paper that a held Series or BioProject links. A build of the same ID already in root is replaced.

Type Description Subset

Raises:

Type Description AccessionError

If an accession is not a GEO Series.

NotAStoreError

If source is not a store, or names no build.

If no Series is listed, the build ID is not a folder name, the source's build is missing, or root may not take the subset (see :func:check_new_root).

def subset(source: Path, series: Iterable[str], root: Path, build_id: str | None = None) -> Subset:
    """Cut the source store's current build to ``series`` and what they link forward to.

    The new build holds the listed Series the source holds, and every record reached from
    them over ``FOLLOWED``, step after step, with the parent of each held BioProject. It
    keeps every link row with a held record at an end, and every link row of a paper that
    a held Series or BioProject links. A build of the same ID already in ``root`` is replaced.

    Parameters
    ----------
    source : pathlib.Path
        The source store's root; only read.
    series : iterable of str
        The GEO Series accessions to keep.
    root : pathlib.Path
        The new root: empty or missing, or a subset of the same source build.
    build_id : str or None
        The new build's ID; defaults to ``<source build ID>-subset``.

    Returns
    -------
    Subset
        What was written.

    Raises
    ------
    AccessionError
        If an accession is not a GEO Series.
    NotAStoreError
        If ``source`` is not a store, or names no build.
    StoreBuildError
        If no Series is listed, the build ID is not a folder name, the source's build is
        missing, or ``root`` may not take the subset (see :func:`check_new_root`).
    """
    listed = _listed(series)
    if not listed:
        raise StoreBuildError("the Series list is empty")
    src = named_build(source, paths.read_marker(source))
    if not src.is_dir():
        raise StoreBuildError(f"the source store's build {src.name} is missing: {src}")
    build_id = build_id or f"{src.name}-subset"
    if Path(build_id).name != build_id or build_id.startswith("."):
        raise StoreBuildError(f"not a build folder name: {build_id!r}")
    check_new_root(root, source, paths.MARKER.rel, src.name, "store")

    out = build_path(root, build_id)
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp = temp_beside(out)
    shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)
    RECORDS.path(tmp).mkdir(parents=True)
    reader = BuildReader(src)
    try:
        held, outside = _write_tables(reader.connection, src, tmp, listed)
        not_held = [a for a in listed if a not in held]
        manifest = layout.manifest_path(src)
        provenance.document_subset(
            tmp,
            build_id,
            src.name,
            json.loads(manifest.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if manifest.is_file() else {},
            series=listed,
            not_held=not_held,
            outside=[{"series": a, "relation": r, "other": b} for a, r, b in outside],
        )
        shutil.rmtree(out, ignore_errors=True)
        tmp.rename(out)
    finally:
        reader.connection.close()
        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)

    if not paths.MARKER.at(root).is_file():
        paths.write_marker(root, {"format_version": FORMAT_VERSION, SUBSET_OF_KEY: src.name})
    paths.switch(root, build_id)
    readme = _write_readme(root, out, src.name, len(listed))
    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
    for kind in held.values():
        counts[kind] = counts.get(kind, 0) + 1
    written = [p for p in out.rglob("*") if p.is_file()] + [paths.MARKER.at(root), readme]
    return Subset(
        build=out,
        source_build=src.name,
        records=dict(sorted(counts.items())),
        not_held=tuple(not_held),
        outside=tuple(outside),
        bytes=sum(p.stat().st_size for p in written),
    )

def init_paper_store(
    root: str | os.PathLike[str],
    *,
    copy_to: str = "",
    drive_remote: str = "",
    drive_folder: str = "",
) -> Path:
    """Make a paper store: its marker and ``README.md``, and the per-user pointer to it.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : str or os.PathLike
        The paper store root; created if missing.
    copy_to : str
        The rclone path the paper store is copied to, ``<remote>:<bucket>/<path>``.
    drive_remote : str
        The rclone remote of the Google Drive that holds the Paperpile folder.
    drive_folder : str
        The Drive ID of the Paperpile folder.

    Returns
    -------
    pathlib.Path
        The marker written.

    Raises
    ------
    LabdataError
        If the root already has a marker, or ``open_store()`` finds no GEO/SRA store.
    """
    open_store()
    path = Path(root).expanduser().absolute()
    path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    marker = path / MARKER
    lines = [
        toml_line("format_version", FORMAT_VERSION),
        toml_line("copy_to", copy_to),
        toml_line("drive_remote", drive_remote),
        toml_line("drive_folder", drive_folder),
    ]
    create_marker(marker, "\n".join(lines) + "\n", "paper store")
    readme = importlib.resources.files("labdata.papers").joinpath("papers_readme.md")
    write_atomic(paths.README.at(path), readme.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    save_pointer(path)
    return marker

items.text:
paper_lock(root: Path) -> Iterator[None]

Hold the paper store's lock, <root>/.lock; a second holder waits for it.

The daily pass and the PMC sync each hold it for their whole run, so they never overlap.

Source code in src/labdata/papers/root.py 
@contextmanager
def paper_lock(root: Path) -> Iterator[None]:
    """Hold the paper store's lock, ``<root>/.lock``; a second holder waits for it.

    The daily pass and the PMC sync each hold it for their whole run, so they never overlap.
    """
    lock = root / LOCK
    with lock.open("a") as fh:
        try:
            fcntl.flock(fh, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
        except BlockingIOError:
            print(f"waiting for {lock}: another paper pass is running", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
            fcntl.flock(fh, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            fcntl.flock(fh, fcntl.LOCK_UN)

Return the paper key of a PMID or DOI, as written in a link or by hand.

A PMID, bare or as PMID:<n>, gives its digits; a DOI, bare, as DOI:<doi> or as a doi.org URL, gives the DOI in lower case.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the text is neither a PMID nor a DOI.

Examples:

>>> paper_key("PMID:39637862"), paper_key("https://doi.org/10.1101/2024.01.15.575678")
('39637862', '10.1101/2024.01.15.575678')
Source code in src/labdata/papers/root.py 
def paper_key(text: str) -> str:
    """Return the paper key of a PMID or DOI, as written in a link or by hand.

    A PMID, bare or as ``PMID:<n>``, gives its digits; a DOI, bare, as ``DOI:<doi>`` or as a
    ``doi.org`` URL, gives the DOI in lower case.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the text is neither a PMID nor a DOI.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> paper_key("PMID:39637862"), paper_key("https://doi.org/10.1101/2024.01.15.575678")
    ('39637862', '10.1101/2024.01.15.575678')
    """
    text = text.strip()
    if m := _PMID.fullmatch(text):
        return m.group(1)
    doi = norm_doi(text)
    if not doi.startswith("10.") or "/" not in doi:
        raise ValueError(f"not a PMID or a DOI: {text!r}")
    return doi

def paper_dir(key: str) -> Path:
    """Return a paper's folder, relative to the paper store root.

    A PMID's folder sits in a group of 1,000, as GEO's FTP groups Series; a DOI's folder is
    the DOI with ``/`` written ``%2F``, so the name converts back.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> paper_dir("39637862").as_posix()
    'papers/39637nnn/39637862'
    >>> paper_dir("10.1101/2024.01.15.575678").as_posix()
    'papers/doi/10.1101%2F2024.01.15.575678'
    """
    if key.isdigit():
        return Path(PAPERS_DIR, f"{key[:-3]}nnn", key)
    return Path(PAPERS_DIR, "doi", urllib.parse.quote(key, safe=""))

items.title: tables
items.text:
The paper store's four tables and the paper files they name: the only code that changes them.

Each table is one Parquet file at the paper store root, sorted by its key columns, in row groups of :data:ROW_GROUP_ROWS rows. A step loads them as :class:PaperTables and changes rows only through its operations, each of which pairs a row change with its file change. A save writes the four tables or none: it writes each to a stage folder, lists them in :data:SAVING, renames them into place, then deletes the list. Loading finishes such a list, then whatever else a stopped step left, so every step starts from a whole store.

@classmethod
def load(cls, root: Path, today: dt.date, *, journal: bool = False) -> PaperTables:
    """Read the paper store at ``root``, first finishing what a stopped step left.

    It finishes a listed save, finishes or drops file moves and deletes by the saved
    ``files`` table, empties the temp folder, then saves the downloads a stopped daily
    pass journaled. The caller holds the paper store's lock.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : pathlib.Path
        The paper store root.
    today : datetime.date
        The UTC date of the step, which journaled downloads are settled for.
    journal : bool
        Journal each file and attempt put before it changes the tables, so a step killed
        before its save loses no download; the save drops the journal.

    Returns
    -------
    PaperTables
        The tables, loaded.
    """
    _finish_save(root)
    state = cls(root)
    state._folder.recover(state.named())
    journaled = root / JOURNAL
    if journaled.is_file():
        state._take_in(journaled.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        state.save(today)
    state._journal = journal
    return state

def drop_papers(self, keys: Collection[str]) -> None:
    """Remove papers from every table, but a paper the ``files`` table lists.

    Its files stay on disk, so its rows stay too: the GCS copy deletes a file its row left.

    Parameters
    ----------
    keys : collection of str
        The papers' keys.
    """
    keys = set(keys) - {f["paper"] for f in self.files}
    for key in keys:
        self._papers.pop(key, None)
        self._info.pop(key, None)
    if keys:
        self._attempts[:] = [a for a in self._attempts if a["paper"] not in keys]

        The key it moves to.
    own_doi : str
        The DOI of ``key``'s paper.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        If the tables hold no paper ``doi``.
    """
    old_row = self._papers.pop(doi)
    self._info.pop(doi, None)
    if key not in self._papers:
        pmid = int(key) if key.isdigit() else None
        self._papers[key] = {**old_row, "paper": key, "pmid": pmid, "doi": own_doi}
    target = self._papers[key]
    target["doi"] = target.get("doi") or own_doi
    others = {*(target.get("other_dois") or ()), *(old_row.get("other_dois") or ()), doi}
    target["other_dois"] = sorted(others - {target["doi"]}) or None
    old_dir, new_dir = paper_dir(doi), paper_dir(key)
    taken = {(f["kind"], f["name"]) for f in self.files if f["paper"] == key}
    for f in [f for f in self.files if f["paper"] == doi]:
        del self._files[_file_key(f)]
        name = f["name"]
        if f["kind"] in ("xml", "pdf") and name.startswith(old_dir.name):
            name = new_dir.name + name[len(old_dir.name) :]
        path = f["path"]
        if (f["kind"], name) in taken:
            if path:
                self._folder.delete(path)
            continue
        if path:
            rel = Path(path).relative_to(old_dir)
            new_path = (
                new_dir / rel.parent / name if f["kind"] != "supplement" else new_dir / rel
            )
            self._folder.move(path, new_path.as_posix())
            path = new_path.as_posix()
        moved = {**f, "paper": key, "name": name, "path": path}
        self._files[_file_key(moved)] = moved
    for attempt in self._attempts:
        if attempt["paper"] == doi:
            attempt["paper"] = key

def write(root: Path, table: PaperTable, rows: Iterable[Mapping[str, Any]]) -> Path:
    """Replace one table with ``rows``, sorted, through a temp file and a rename.

    The same rows, in any order, give the same file. A write stopped before the rename
    leaves the old table in place.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : pathlib.Path
        The paper store root.
    table : PaperTable
        One of :data:`TABLES`.
    rows : iterable of mapping
        Every row of the new table, keyed by column name; a missing column is null.

    Returns
    -------
    pathlib.Path
        The table's file.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a row names an unknown column, has no ``paper``, repeats a key, or holds a value
        outside a column's fixed vocabulary.
    """
    names = set(table.schema.names)
    checked = []
    for row in rows:
        unknown = set(row) - names
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(f"{table.name}: unknown columns {sorted(unknown)}")
        if not row.get("paper"):
            raise ValueError(f"{table.name}: a row has no paper: {dict(row)}")
        for column, values in (table.allowed or {}).items():
            if row.get(column) is not None and row[column] not in values:
                raise ValueError(f"{table.name}: {column} {row[column]!r} is not one of {values}")
        checked.append(row)
    data = pa.Table.from_pylist(checked, schema=table.schema).sort_by(
        [(c, "ascending") for c in table.sort_by]
    )
    if table.key:
        keys = list(zip(*(data.column(c).to_pylist() for c in table.key), strict=True))
        if len(set(keys)) != len(keys):
            raise ValueError(f"{table.name}: a row's {', '.join(table.key)} appears twice")
    path = table.path(root)
    tmp = temp_beside(path)
    try:
        pq.write_table(
            data, tmp, row_group_size=ROW_GROUP_ROWS, compression="zstd", compression_level=3
        )
        tmp.replace(path)
    finally:
        tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    return path

def read_status(root: Path) -> PaperStatus:
    """Return the paper store's status; an empty one before the first pass.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : pathlib.Path
        The paper store root.

    Returns
    -------
    PaperStatus
        The status; keys the file holds that ``PaperStatus`` lacks are ignored.

    path = root / STATUS

    data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    names = {f.name for f in fields(PaperStatus)}

def paper(self, key: str) -> Paper:
    """Return one paper: its IDs, status, details and files.

    ----------

    ValueError
        If ``key`` is neither a PMID nor a DOI.

        If the paper store does not hold the paper.

    wanted = paper_key(key)

def papers(self, keys: Iterable[str]) -> dict[str, Paper]:
    """Return many papers, reading each table once; use it to walk many papers.

    Parameters
    ----------
    keys : iterable of str
        PMIDs, bare or as ``PMID:<n>``, or DOIs, as :meth:`paper` takes them.

    Returns
    -------
    dict of str to Paper
        Each held key, as :func:`~labdata.papers.root.paper_key` gives it, in input
        order, mapped to its paper; a key the store does not hold is left out.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a key is neither a PMID nor a DOI.
    """
    wanted = list(dict.fromkeys(paper_key(k) for k in keys))
    if not wanted:
        return {}
    dois = {w for w in wanted if not w.isdigit()}
    rows = self._paper_rows(wanted, dois)
    by_key = {r["paper"]: r for r in rows}
    by_doi = _by_doi(rows)
    hits = {w: row for w in wanted if (row := by_key.get(w) or by_doi.get(w))}
    held = {row["paper"] for row in hits.values()}
    info = {r["paper"]: r for r in self._rows(tables.PAPER_INFO, held)} if held else {}
    files: dict[str, list[PaperFile]] = {}
    for f in self._rows(tables.FILES, held) if held else []:
        files.setdefault(f["paper"], []).append(_file(self.root, f))
    return {
        w: Paper(
            key=row["paper"],
            status=row["status"],
            reason=row["reason"],
            pmid=row["pmid"],
            pmcid=row["pmcid"],
            doi=row["doi"],
            openalex=row["openalex"],
            published=row["published"],
            xml_tier=row["xml_tier"],
            pdf_tier=row["pdf_tier"],
            info=_info(info[row["paper"]]) if row["paper"] in info else None,
            files=tuple(files.get(row["paper"], ())),
        )
        for w, row in hits.items()
    }

def papers_for(self, accessions: Iterable[str]) -> dict[str, PaperLinks]:
    """Map each Series or BioProject to the papers its build links, with their status.

    A DOI link counts only when the paper store holds its paper. A PMID link counts
    before the paper store takes the paper in, unless it is a placeholder.

    Parameters
    ----------
    accessions : iterable of str
        GEO Series and BioProject accessions, in the order wanted back.

    Returns
    -------
    dict of str to PaperLinks
        Each accession, in input order, mapped to its linked papers; an empty
        ``papers`` means "no paper linked".

    Raises
    ------
    AccessionError
        If an accession is malformed.
    """
    order = [a.strip().upper() for a in accessions]
    for accession in order:
        kind_of(accession)
    targets: dict[str, dict[str, set[str]]] = {a: {} for a in order}
    for src, dst, _relation, source in self.build.links(set(order)) if order else []:
        if src in targets and dst.startswith((_PMID, _DOI)) and _is_paper(dst):
            targets[src].setdefault(dst, set()).add(source)
    linked = {t for ts in targets.values() for t in ts}
    pmids = {paper_key(t) for t in linked if t.startswith(_PMID)}
    dois = {paper_key(t) for t in linked if t.startswith(_DOI)}
    rows = self._paper_rows(pmids | dois, dois) if pmids | dois else []
    by_key = {r["paper"]: r for r in rows}
    by_doi = _by_doi(rows)
    out = {}
    for accession in order:
        found: dict[str, LinkedPaper] = {}
        for target, sources in targets[accession].items():
            key = paper_key(target)
            row = by_key.get(key) or by_doi.get(key)
            if row is not None:
                found[row["paper"]] = LinkedPaper(row["paper"], row["status"], row["reason"])
            elif target.startswith(_PMID) and not is_placeholder(key, sources):
                found[key] = LinkedPaper(key, None, None)
        out[accession] = PaperLinks(accession, tuple(found[k] for k in sorted(found)))
    return out
